summary: Pend Oreille County, WA: 1937 10-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, removed or destroyed in the 1950s; no source describes what remains on the summit.

visit.trail_note: Willhite: drive a gravel road to its end (high clearance advised), then walk about 0.25 miles one way, gaining 150 feet, partly bushwhacking. The road ends in a different place than the map shows.

events.note: Decade only: 1950s. The Register says removed; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. The Forest Lookouts page lists it as removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the tower was removed in the 1950s. firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed in that decade. The story reports both words.
The Register gives 3,770 ft (1,149 m); Willhite gives 3,778 feet. The story gives both and uses the Register's figure as the primary value.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: status gone, Pend Oreille County, coordinates, elevation (3,770 ft = 1149.1 m) and FFLOS registration all agree; no corrections. Only the Willhite page describes the approach and the summit, and no source found names any staff or fire, so the story has no staffing or fire section. The 1950s date is decade-only, so the event year is a placeholder 1950 and the note says so. The access level is deliberately omitted: the route is described, but no source says whether the site is open, and Colville National Forest status is not stated in terms. What remains on the summit is not described by any source read; Willhite's 2024 summit photos have no text. Used 1 WebSearch (no new Dry Canyon source) and 5 distinct pages, under the per-tower budget.
